decisions.statement: More than a second of work on the extension host's thread locks the editor up.
Enough watch events arriving together ends the extension host.
A panel or a tab or the status line reads one file and works nothing out from the repository.
That file is written by one service rather than by the editor.
A panel or a tab or the status line re-reads when its own file is written.
A file's cooldown lands the first change at once and collects the rest for its own wait.
The editor is a fork of openvscode-server never rebased onto openvscode-server.
The editor runs as a desktop application.
The editor is served to a browser only to run the editor's own checks.
A seat works in the `code-editor` checkout.
A candidate works in a worktree of the `code-editor` checkout.
Alan runs an artefact under `~/.local/share`.
Only the editor's own `tools/promote.sh` writes the artefact Alan runs.
A change to the fork reaches Alan only once the fork is promoted.
The artefact's `extensions/ops` is a symlink to `editor-extension` in akasha.
A change to the extension reaches Alan without being promoted.
A change reaches Alan's window only on a window reload.
A read that failed leaves the last good rows on screen.
A panel counts every row of every kind the panel showed.
A panel showing an agent's color follows that agent's turn state as the state changes.
A turn state is shown within 100ms of the file with the state being written.
The work panel's top row holds the initiatives under no other initiative.
The initiatives under that top row are ordered alphabetically by slug.
A row with a seat of its own takes that seat's color.
Green outranks blue.
Blue outranks yellow.
Yellow outranks every other color.
A color the ranking does not name sits below every color the ranking names.
An act on a seat runs `ops` directly rather than through a shell.
A terminal the seat menu opens does nothing but attach to a seat.
Changing where a seat runs leaves the agent in that seat untouched.
Running a seat interactively gives the seat a terminal Alan can watch.
Running a seat headless takes the seat's terminal away.
Stopping a seat ends the agent in the seat.
Resuming a seat returns a stopped seat on the session the seat was bound to.
Resetting a seat replaces the agent in the seat with a new agent.
Copying a seat name puts that name on the clipboard.
Alan works in the editor rather than in desktop VS Code.
Parts of the upstream fork Alan will never use have been removed.
Any agent can arrange the editor's tabs.
Any agent can arrange the editor's groups.
Any agent can arrange the editor's panels.
The editor's build resolves the dependencies the build needs inside the editor's own checkout.
No code repository sits beside the editor's build.
The editor is one clone.
A row in the work panel is the top row, an initiative, or an intent that initiative has.
An initiative's intents are drawn beneath that initiative.
An intent is drawn in the place its initiative states rather than sorted.
An intent opens the page of the initiative with that intent.
An initiative is assigned to the seat its name begins with from the work panel.
That seat takes the initiative only where the seat has a page and is running.
An initiative that seat already answers to is no reason to refuse.
The item is offered on every initiative and refuses where the seat is away.
Every act the seat menu names is offered in the seat menu.

definition: a workbench of files, groups, panels and terminals
